clue.text: Sale being in two parts is of no consequence

indicators.note: being in two parts says the word Sale is to be split, each part described by one word of the answer

parts.note: split into S and ALE: S is the abbreviation for small and ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A shop's sale that is split into two halves turns out to be unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's two words, read as wordplay, rebuild SALE, as S (small) followed by ALE (beer). 'Small beer' is British idiom for something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a trivial matter, originally weak, low-alcohol ale, so it means something unimportant.

clue.text: Watch out for broadcast as such waters may be dangerous

definitions.text: as such waters may be dangerous

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so we go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: to mind something is to watch out for it, as in 'mind the step'

explanation.surface: A warning to look out for something on the radio, because certain waters are hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: MIND and MINED are said the same way. 'Broadcast' looks like the thing to watch out for, but it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters seeded with explosive sea mines are dangerous to shipping; such waters are described as mined.

clue.text: Deplore Lithuania's housing? So be it!

indicators.note: Lithuania's code is housing, holding another word inside it

parts.note: LT is the international code for Lithuania
amen means 'so be it' at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans the state of Lithuania's homes, then resigns themselves to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' reads as dwellings belonging to Lithuania, but it is the verb that places AMEN between L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to mourn or regret it aloud, a synonym of deploring it.

clue.text: A social climber raised one plant

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a snob is someone who tries to climb the social ladder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A status-seeker brought up a single potted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree grown in a pot, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Rock up half-heartedly for a joint

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom
the word's heart is its doubled middle letter, and only half of that pair is kept

parts.note: to rock is to wobble

explanation.surface: Someone turns up feeling lukewarm, ready to share a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one B from WOBBLE to leave WOBLE, and 'up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge between upper arm and forearm, an anatomical joint.

clue.text: Amazed to see fat gets beard messy

parts.note: flab is body fat

indicators.note: messy means the letters of these words are in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to see a fat man's beard getting untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' looks like a description of the beard, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'gets beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flabbergasted is to be astonished or dumbfounded, a stronger synonym for amazed.

clue.text: Following article by Vogue to some degree, but not very well

definitions.text: to some degree, but not very well

parts.note: after means following
a is the indefinite article
vogue means fashion, as in 'in vogue'

explanation.surface: Something follows an article in Vogue magazine, and only partly succeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue looks like the magazine's name, but it is just the word for a current fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something after a fashion means doing it in a rough, passable way that falls short of competence.

clue.text: Screen enthusiast taking in, perhaps, Douglas's The Game

indicators.note: taking in means the outer words hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: a blind is a window screen
a buff is an enthusiast, as in a film buff
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, so its island's possessive is MAN'S; 'perhaps' marks that Douglas is just one example

explanation.surface: A film fan watches Michael Douglas starring in the thriller The Game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the actor Michael Douglas and his film The Game; here Douglas is the Isle of Man's capital, a British island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind man's buff is a traditional children's party game in which a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.

clue.text: The man will be a pain about English growth

indicators.note: about means the words placed round another piece

parts.note: HE'LL is short for 'he will'
to bore is to be tedious, a pain

explanation.surface: A man warns he will be tiresome on the subject of English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be a pain' is read as a verb, to bore; 'about' wraps the two words round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebore is a flowering plant, such as the Christmas rose; growth here is a loose word for a plant.

clue.text: Exploit first appearance on river

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or first appearance
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone makes use of a debut on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' looks like a verb but is the noun, a daring deed. The Ure is a North Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold feat or escapade, a close synonym of an adventure.

clue.text: Implant educated European doctor introduces

indicators.note: introduces means these pieces go before the next one

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An educated European physician introduces an implant.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly within a surrounding mass, which is what implanting does.

clue.text: Bond keeps one for exercise

indicators.note: keeps means the outer word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: to weld is to bond metal pieces
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: James Bond saves one session for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' is a verb here, as in exercising power.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield authority or influence is to exercise it, to put it to use.

clue.text: What about time in charge of moral code?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: eh? is said for 'what?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what time the person in charge of ethics arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, as in the work ethic.

clue.text: Looking at following orders without objection

indicators.note: without means the next piece is taken away

parts.note: obeying means following orders
OB is a recognised abbreviation for objection

explanation.surface: A soldier watching while carrying out commands without complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it, so eying is a synonym for looking at.

clue.text: Peeled onion can produce such a welcome

indicators.note: peeled means the outer skin, the first and last letters, is removed

parts.note: a shallot is a small onion

explanation.surface: An onion's peel releases a smell that greets you.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is a variant spelling of hello, a spoken greeting.

clue.text: Parliament vacated after scream in vault

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the previous one

parts.note: to cry is to scream

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A scream rings out in a vault after Parliament has emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber or vault beneath a church.

clue.text: Flexibility means going after fish from the east

indicators.note: going after means this piece follows the previous one
reading from the east in an across clue means right to left

parts.note: the eel is a fish
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Easing up means pursuing fish from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, a margin of freedom or flexibility.

clue.text: Sack Republican and "regular Joe" voter ultimately leaving

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart

parts.note: regular means ordinary or average

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words Joe and voter

explanation.surface: An American election story: a Republican and an ordinary 'regular Joe' voter quit at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'regular Joe' look like one phrase, but 'regular' alone gives AVERAGE and 'ultimately' takes the last letters of Joe and voter, ER, which 'leaving' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town in war is to plunder and devastate it, the same as ravaging it.

clue.text: Song on popular set

indicators.note: on in an across clue means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: in means popular, as in the in thing
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A tune plays on a popular TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: To inlay is to set pieces of material into a surface for decoration.

clue.text: Fine for the French keeping our island landmark

indicators.note: keeping means the outer word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: bien is French for fine or well
GB, Great Britain, is the island of the setter and his British readers

explanation.surface: French visitors praise a British landmark they get to keep.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell, and loosely the clock tower, of the Houses of Parliament in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The clock tower at Westminster is one of London's most famous landmarks.

clue.text: Aesthetic movement offering role outside work

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An art movement offers an actor a role away from the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art was the 1950s and 60s art movement drawing on mass culture, such as Warhol's soup cans.

clue.text: Suggestion from good master of ceremonies

parts.note: a host presents an event, acting as master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: A hint offered by a capable compère.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost of something is a faint trace or hint, as in the ghost of a smile.

clue.text: Staff supporting strike is a killer

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means this piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: to hit is to strike
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An employee backing a walkout turns out to be a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a hired assassin, someone paid to kill.

clue.text: Nasty smell clears up before church

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the next
up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: to net a sum is to clear it as profit

explanation.surface: A foul odour lifts before the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clears' looks like the smell dispersing, but it means earns as profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, offensive odour.

clue.text: Some, for a start, dreaded disciple

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: For starters, some followers are feared.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is a follower of the Rastafari faith, often wearing dreadlocks, hence a dreadlocked disciple.

clue.text: Share national boxing stadium

indicators.note: boxing means these words enclose the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A national share of a boxing stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport, but it is the signal that the words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or entertainment, a stadium.

clue.text: Escort drug dealers before stripping

indicators.note: stripping means removing the outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: pushers are drug dealers

explanation.surface: An escort agency's drug dealers before a strip show.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, escorting them.

clue.text: Free link needing it to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means turned upwards, so the two letters spelling it are flipped

parts.note: to unite things is to link them

explanation.surface: A free connection demands that it be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to release or set it free from a knot or bond.

clue.text: Decision put off people crossing major route

indicators.note: crossing means these words span the next piece, which sits between them

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a nation is a people
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A decision is postponed for people crossing a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; as letters it becomes MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination can mean the settling of a question, a decision or ruling.

clue.text: Sailing ship may have this power source and energy in the supply

parts.note: the mains is the domestic electricity supply

indicators.note: supply is read as supple, bendy, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailing ship might run on mains power with energy in its supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but it is the adverb of supple, the signal to rearrange E and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsheet is the rope used to control the angle of a sailing vessel's mainsail.
